title: Dimension of a formal monoid ring and a parameter hypersurface
statement:
Let $(D,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $T$ a fine saturated sharp monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively; sharp means that its only invertible element is $0$. Let $D[T]$ be the ring with $D$-basis $[t]$, $t\in T$, and multiplication $[t][u]=[t+u]$. Put $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m,[t]:t\ne0)\subset D[T]$, let $H=\varprojlim_jD[T]/\mathfrak a^j$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $L=([t]:t\in T\setminus\{0\})H$. Then $H$ is a Noetherian local integral domain, $H/L\cong D$, and
$$\dim H=\dim D+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}.$$
Furthermore, for every $\eta\in H$ whose reduction $\overline\eta\in H/L=D$ belongs to $\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$, multiplication by $\eta$ on $H$ is injective, $D/(\overline\eta)$ is regular local, and
$$\dim(H/(\eta))=\dim D+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}-1,\qquad \dim(D/(\overline\eta))=\dim D-1.$$
Dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; the zero-rank monoid $T=\{0\}$ is allowed.

proof.text: Put $d=\dim D$, $G=T^{\rm gp}$ and $r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}G$. Fineness makes $T$ finitely generated. If $u+v=0$, both terms are units, hence zero by sharpness; thus $\{0\}$ is a face. For this face, [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] has $Q_F=R=T$ and gives $T\hookrightarrow G\cong\mathbf Z^r$. Inside $G$, $t,-t\in T$ makes $t$ a unit, hence $T\cap(-T)=\{0\}$. Apply [lem-trf-sharp-monoid-positive-grading] to obtain a positive weight $w$. Choose nonzero generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $T$, allowing $s=0$. The map $D[X_1,\ldots,X_s]\to D[T]$, $X_i\mapsto[g_i]$, is surjective since each basis monomial is a product of generators. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] make $H$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $D$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 0316, lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian; VI 1.6 coefficient refinement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-residue-domain] to $A=D$, $P=T$ and $w$. Its hypotheses hold by completeness of $D$ and step 1. It gives a constant-coefficient map $c:H\to D$ with kernel $L$, the canonical isomorphism $H/L\cong D$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak aH=c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$, and the domain property of $H$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, agent-supplied coefficient-algebra refinement: constant-coefficient kernel, geometric-series locality, and least-monomial domain argument (old proof steps 3--4 of lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension).

proof.text: Since $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak aH$, its powers are $\mathfrak n^n=\mathfrak a^nH$. By [lem-trf-formal-monoid-length-filtration], all coefficient quotient lengths $\lambda(k)=\mathrm{length}_D(D/\mathfrak m^k)$ are finite, and $\mathrm{length}_H(H/\mathfrak n^n)=\sum_{\nu(t)<n}\lambda(n-\nu(t))$. Regard these finite lengths as nonnegative real numbers. The function $\lambda$ is nondecreasing: a submodule chain lifts along each quotient surjection. By [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] for $D$, its eventual polynomial has degree $d$ and positive leading coefficient, so $\lambda(k)$ lies between positive multiples of $k^d$ for large $k$. The subgroup generated by $T$ is $G$; apply [lem-trf-positive-monoid-length-growth] to bound the displayed sum between positive multiples of $n^{d+r}$. Apply the same Hilbert--Samuel node to the nonzero Noetherian local ring $H$. A polynomial of degree $e$ with positive leading coefficient grows between positive multiples of $n^e$; comparison forces $e=d+r$. Hence $\dim H=d+r$. The growth node includes $r=0$, with $T=\{0\}$ and the sum equal to $\lambda(n)$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, with Tag 00K8; elementary lower monomial count and comparison of polynomial degrees.

proof.text: Put $f=c(\eta)\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$. Then $f\ne0$, so $\eta\ne0$; the domain property makes multiplication by $\eta$ injective. Also $\eta\in c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to $H,\eta$ to get $\dim(H/(\eta))+1=d+r$, and to the domain $D$ and its nonzero element $f$ to get $\dim(D/(f))+1=d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion], $D/(f)$ is regular local. These give the assertions; when $d=0$, $\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$ is empty.

lean.statement: theorem formalMonoidRing_dimension (D : Type u) [CommRing D] [IsRegularLocalRing D] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal D) D] (T : Type v) [AddCommMonoid T] (hfs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Multiplicative T)) (hsharp : ∀ t : T, IsUnit (Multiplicative.ofAdd t) → t = 0) (a : Ideal (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) (ha : a = Ideal.map (algebraMap D (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal D) ⊔ Ideal.span {b | ∃ t : T, t ≠ 0 ∧ b = single t (1 : D)}) (L : Ideal (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T))) (hL : L = Ideal.span {b | ∃ t : T, t ≠ 0 ∧ b = AdicCompletion.of a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T) (single t (1 : D))}) : IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) ∧ IsLocalRing (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) ∧ IsDomain (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) ∧ ringKrullDim (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) = ringKrullDim D + (Cardinal.toENat (Module.rank ℚ (TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (Additive (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (Multiplicative T))))) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∃ e : (AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T) ⧸ L) ≃ₐ[D] D, ∀ η : AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T), e (Ideal.Quotient.mk L η) ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal D → e (Ideal.Quotient.mk L η) ∉ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal D) ^ 2 → Function.Injective (fun x : AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T) => η * x) ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (D ⧸ Ideal.span {e (Ideal.Quotient.mk L η)}) ∧ ringKrullDim ((AdicCompletion a (AddMonoidAlgebra D T)) ⧸ Ideal.span {η}) + 1 = ringKrullDim D + (Cardinal.toENat (Module.rank ℚ (TensorProduct ℤ ℚ (Additive (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (Multiplicative T))))) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ringKrullDim (D ⧸ Ideal.span {e (Ideal.Quotient.mk L η)}) + 1 = ringKrullDim D
